html:
The Guam Organic Act, signed in 1950, made the people of Guam citizens of the United States and set up a civilian government with an elected legislature, ending navy rule.

Chamorro leaders had pressed for this for decades, and walked out of their advisory assembly in 1949 in protest. The act came after the war, during which Chamorros had stayed loyal to the US.

Guam remains an unincorporated territory: its people cannot vote for president and have a non-voting delegate in Congress. The military holds much of the island, and questions of land and of Chamorro self-determination are still open. Compare American Samoa.
sum: The Guam Organic Act, signed in 1950, made the people of Guam citizens of the United States and set up a civilian government with an elected legislature, ending navy rule.
